To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The beta to gamma-1CaO.2SiO2 transformation can successfully be suppressed by high cooling rate and that the resulting end product is a hydraulic binder upon mixing with water; 2) The mechanical activation of steel slag via high energy milling is an effective method of increasing the hydraulic activity of the as-received material; 3) A hydration behavior is proposed for the major slag components.
the hydraulic properties of secondary steelmaking slag can be improved by: a) rapid cooling and b) mechanical milling.

a) the beta to gamma2CaO.Sio2 transformation can be prevented by rapid cooling, and the end product is a hydraulically active material upon mixing with water; and b) the hydraulic activity of the slag can be increased by mechanical activation, and this effect is more pronounced at higher milling times.

the transformation of secondary steelmaking slag into a cementitious material by means of controlled cooling and mechanical activation.
the development of a sustainable, cementitious binder from secondary steelmaking slag.
